sensors.name: light sensor LLIGHT (light from above, dim only inside a tunnel)

control_flow: Forever: call followLine. If the left light sensor reads below 50 %, curve left; else curve right.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads below 50 %

branches.outcome: bright (50 % or more): it curves right

scenarios.coded_response: The light is 100 % in the open, so the condition is never true: it curves right (left wheel 40 %, right wheel 10 %) again and again and circles. No block reads the line tracker.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a black line in bright light, facing along it
scenarios.title: Follows the line
assumptions: The end of the line is where the robot should get to.
You didn't say where on the line the robot starts.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line to its end

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left (left wheel 10 %, right wheel 40 %) again and again
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is deep inside a tunnel, in dim light, with nothing in front of it
scenarios.trigger: The left light sensor reads below 50 %
scenarios.title: Curves left in dim light

uncertainties: Your program reads the left light sensor, which looks up, not the line tracker: it cannot see a line, and on a plain bright floor it curves right all the time.
The light falls below 50 % only about 12.5 cm inside a tunnel's roof, so the left curve happens only in dim light there.
You said nothing about what the robot should do in dim light, so there is no expected behaviour for that situation.

outcomes.words: the condition doesn't hold: the else part runs
planned: Follows the line in the open
